question: What is the meaning of deconstructability in relation to sustainability features?
description: Deconstructability refers to the ability of building parts to be dismantled, which supports a sustainable end-of-life scenario for building components. It is based on two factors: ratio of demountable connections and ratio of prefabricated building elements. Demountable connections stimulate a circular building that can be dismantled and reused, while fixed connections allow only a demolition scenario. The deconstructability score (D-score) is calculated based on these factors, with a greater value indicating higher deconstructability. This feature is important for sustainability as it enables material recovery and reduces waste generation.
